BEFORE THE
                     FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION



In the Matter of the Application of:                 )
                                                     )
DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC                    )           Docket No. P-15424-000




                         CENTER FOR BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
                              MOTION TO INTERVENE

       Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”) Rules of

Practice and Procedure, the Center for Biological Diversity (“Center”) moves to intervene in the

proceeding regarding the DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC preliminary permit application

for the proposed DeepGreen Western Passage Subsea-Compute & Infrastructure Hub

(“Project”). 18 C.F.R. § 385.214. By this motion, the Center seeks to ensure that wildlife,

including North Atlantic right whales, fin whales, and their habitats are protected and to pursue

the public interest as FERC evaluates the application.

                                 CONTACT INFORMATION

       All filings, orders, and correspondence respecting these proceedings and this intervention

should be sent to:

       Miyoko Sakashita
       Center for Biological Diversity
       2100 Franklin St., Suite 375

    I.      DESCRIPTION OF INTERVENOR

        This intervention motion is filed on behalf of the Center for Biological Diversity

(“Center”). The Center is a 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation with offices nationwide. The Center

advocates for biodiversity protection through science, policy, and law. The Center has programs

focused specifically on endangered species, ocean protection, and public lands, among others.

We have more than 1.8 million members and supporters, including members in Maine and

throughout New England, who use and enjoy coastal and marine areas for wildlife observation,

recreation, scientific study, and aesthetic enjoyment.

        The Center has a long-standing interest in conserving wildlife in the Atlantic Ocean and

has worked for decades to protect critically endangered North Atlantic right whales and their

habitat, along with other whales such as fin and humpback whales. Its work includes advocacy to

secure and defend critical habitat for North Atlantic right whales; reduce vessel-strikes of large

whales; reduce entanglements in fishing gear of fin whales, humpback whales, minke whales,

and right whales; and address ocean noise, which can harm all marine mammals. The Center’s

members use the coast and waters off Maine to sail, kayak, photograph, study, and view whales,

seabirds, fish, and other marine wildlife.

        The Center and its members may be adversely affected by the outcome of this

proceeding. The Project is proposed for 27.1 acres in Western Passage near Eastport, within the

Bay of Fundy, which is used by North Atlantic right whales, minke whales, fin whales,

humpback whales and other marine animals. Preliminary studies, construction, and operation of

the underwater energy-generation facility and data center could increase vessel traffic and

underwater noise, disturb whales and their prey, alter marine habitat, and create collision or

Motion to Intervene
2 of 8
 displacement risks. These effects could impair members’ ability to observe, study, photograph,

and otherwise enjoy wildlife and the Bay of Fundy ecosystem. The Center therefore has a direct

interest in preventing and mitigating those harms.

    II.      THE PROPOSED PROJECT

          On February 11, 2026, DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC (“DeepGreen”) filed an

application with FERC for a preliminary permit to study the feasibility of the DeepGreen

Western Passage Subsea-Compute & Infrastructure Hub, Project No. 15424-000. The Project

was amended on July 30, 2026. The Project would be located in Western Passage of the Bay of

Fundy near Eastport, Maine. FERC issued a notice of the accepted application on August 25,

2026. 1

          The preliminary-permit stage includes surveys and studies in preparation for pilot and

commercial phases. At this initial stage, DeepGreen intends to conduct high-resolution

bathymetric and geophysical surveys, mapping, year-round environmental monitoring,

interconnection studies, and other studies. These activities would prepare for Phase 1, the

Project’s 27.1-acre pilot phase, which would generate 1 to 5 megawatts of energy from up to 16

tidal turbines to power a 34 subsea data-center pods and would include a 1.5-mile cable to shore

and supporting facilities. The Phase 2 commercial expansion could extend the Project to as much

as 400 acres, add up to 34 tidal turbines producing 10 to 15 megawatts of energy, and include an

unspecified number of subsea data-center pods.

     III.       GROUNDS FOR INTERVENTION

           The Center has and represents interests that may be directly affected by the outcome of

the proceeding, and the Center’s participation is also in the public interest. Under FERC Rule

214, a party seeking intervention must state, “to the extent known,” its position and the basis in

fact and law for that position. 2 The party must also demonstrate an interest that may be directly

affected by the outcome or that its participation is in the public interest. 3 This motion is timely

because it is submitted on or before the October 19, 2026, deadline established in FERC’s

notice. 4

           The Center has members and staff who reside on and visit the Maine coast. They use and

enjoy coastal and marine waters to sail, kayak, photograph, study, and seek to view North

Atlantic right whales, fin whales, and other species. Members have aesthetic and recreational

interests in marine life and in the healthy marine ecosystems on which they depend. The Center

has worked for more than two decades to protect the critically endangered North Atlantic right

whale. In 2005, it petitioned for stronger Endangered Species Act protections and later sought

expanded habitat protections for the whales. The Center has also repeatedly petitioned and

litigated to strengthen federal vessel-speed rules to prevent vessel strikes of right whales, rules

that also benefit fin whales and humpback whales. The Center has also advocated to protect right

whales, as well as humpback whales, fin whales, and minke whales, from deadly fishing-gear

entanglements, including through service on the Atlantic Large Whale Take Reduction Team.

 The Center works to protect other wildlife in the Atlantic and Maine, including endangered

Atlantic salmon, Atlantic sturgeon, bluefin tuna, other marine mammals, fish, and seabirds.

       The proposed activities could increase risks to North Atlantic right whales and other

species in the region. Western Passage is a biologically productive, high-current marine

environment connected to the Bay of Fundy. For example, North Atlantic right whales use the

Bay of Fundy as a traditional feeding and nursing habitat, and protecting these waters is

important to the species’ survival and recovery. The proposed activities would increase vessel

traffic, underwater noise, and habitat disturbance and could reduce prey availability, adversely

affecting right whales and their habitat. These industrial activities could also adversely affect fin

whales, humpback whales, seals, fish, seabirds, and other marine animals.




A right whale named “Epic” had its head covered with reddish-brown mud from the Bay of
Fundy. Credit: NOAA Fisheries/Alison Ogilvie

Motion to Intervene
5 of 8
          Activities during the preliminary-permit stage may harm the Center’s interests. High-

resolution surveys and monitoring may increase vessel traffic and noise pollution from the use of

echosounders, sonar, or other survey equipment. These activities may disrupt the behavior of

right whales, fin whales, and other marine wildlife, interfere with communication and foraging,

affect prey, increase pollution, and impair habitat. If built, the Project would amplify those risks

and raise additional concerns, including entrapment, thermal discharges, contaminants, noise,

and construction impacts.

         In short, the Center and its members have a substantial interest in participating in FERC’s

review of the Project and its potential effects on North Atlantic right whales, fin whales,

humpback whales, other marine wildlife, fisheries, habitats, water quality, cultural resources, and

public uses of Western Passage and the Bay of Fundy.

   IV.        STATEMENT OF POSITION

         The Center seeks to participate in this proceeding to ensure that public-resource values,

including conservation of North Atlantic right whales, fin whales, humpback whales and their

habitats as well as other marine wildlife, are protected. The Center also seeks to ensure that any

authorization of the Project complies with all applicable state and federal environmental laws.

         The Center opposes the proposed preliminary permit due to concerns about the potential

impacts on North Atlantic right whales, fin whales, humpback whales, and other wildlife and the

integrity of the ecosystems upon which they depend. The Center aims to protect the public

interest and ensure compliance with environmental laws. The Center reserves the right to modify

or further develop its position as additional information becomes available.


Motion to Intervene
6 of 8
    V.      CONCLUSION

        Because the Center has substantial interests in this proceeding and in the Project’s

potential effects on Western Passage, the Bay of Fundy, and their wildlife and habitats,

intervention is necessary for the Center to represent those interests and seek to avoid and

mitigate harm. Those interests are not adequately represented by any other party. The Center

respectfully requests that FERC grant its motion to intervene in the DeepGreen Western Passage

Subsea-Compute & Infrastructure Hub, Project No. P-15424-000.

DATED: September 24, 2026
